properties.description:
DELIVERED 2026-08-18 in the `where-am-i` skill (PR #246), then REVISED the same day (`epoch:the-ask-elicits-a-lens-not-a-name`). Source is `getting-started/skills/where-am-i/SKILL.md`, mirrored byte-identically to `.claude/` and `.grok/`, all three enforced by `skill_lint`. **This is the DELIVERY; `req:the-agent-learns-who-it-is-talking-to` states what is owed, and `dec:idea-a-user-carries-a-persona-that-shapes-every-reply` still asks whether a stored persona is the right long-term mechanism.**

WHAT SHIPPED:
1. **A "Who you are talking to" step** before the design is read back. It asks once, records the answer via `add_contributor`'s `description` **in the reader's own words**, and does NOT ask again when one is recorded. A guess from a login or git author is an OFFER and never a silent default. The answer shapes speech but never the record.
2. **The hardcoded audience removed.** The instruction read *"Write it as prose for the person who described this project to you"* — false for exactly the newcomer this serves.
3. **A register rule** under "Keep it honest", stating the vocabulary-swap distinction: reflow2's own words (gap, loop, detector) dropped; a systems engineer's words (requirement, interface, verification) KEPT, because softening them is condescension.

⭐⭐ **THE REVISION, AND WHY THE FIRST VERSION WAS NOT GOOD ENOUGH.** It asked *"who am I talking to, and what do you work in?"* — and **"Bob" answers that correctly while telling the agent nothing.** Anthony caught it the day it shipped. The ask now:
  · **requests a BACKGROUND, not an identity** — what they do day to day AND what they trained in;
  · **carries an example of a useful answer inside the question** (*"software engineer, but my degree is in biology"*), because an example shapes a reply far more reliably than an instruction to answer fully;
  · **explains that the two halves diverge and that the divergence is the point**, with three worked cases of how a background changes which explanation lands;
  · **gives a thin answer ONE follow-up and then stops** — an opening courtesy, not an intake form;
  · **keeps listening afterwards**, because people show their vocabulary by using it and a background written once goes stale like any other fact.

🛑 **STATUS IS `realized`, NOT `verified`.** `skill_lint` proves the prose is present, mirrored and references only real tools. **It does not prove the behaviour happens.** The scoped gap pass classifies this correctly as `component_granularity_verification` — a real check one hop away at `cmp:skills`, shared by ten capabilities. The route to its own proof already exists in shape: `skill_lint` asserts *no served skill hardcodes a particular answer language*; the sibling — **no served skill hardcodes an AUDIENCE** — would have caught the defect in (2) and would keep it caught. Named, not built.

⚠️ TO BE REVISED, 2026-09-28, under dec:idea-a-user-carries-a-persona-that-shapes-every-reply (settled on @ajs's word). where-am-i's ask survives, but its answer is no longer written into the design's Contributor. It is used from, or saved to, the host or the agent's own memory. The where-am-i skill text and the served lens line change with it.

REVISED 2026-09-30 (chg:the-served-text-keeps-the-readers-lens-out-of-the-design), under req:a-design-holds-who-contributed-never-a-readers-persona: where-am-i's ask survives and its answer is no longer written into the design. The step now takes the reader's lens from the host, else the agent's own memory, else the person's own words with at most one question, and keeps the answer out of the design; item 1 of WHAT SHIPPED above ("records the answer via add_contributor's description") no longer holds. The several-people clause (git-author match, offered in one sentence, attributed to) now serves attribution. req:the-agent-learns-who-it-is-talking-to keeps its TO BE REVISED note, which waits for @ajs's word. Delivered with cap:the-served-text-applies-the-readers-lens-without-writing-it-into-the-design.
properties.name: Orientation asks what lens the reader brings, once, and matches their vocabulary from then on
